note: A reading, not the text's statement. FOR: the New Testament reads the Hebrew Bible's Spirit as the Holy Spirit: "The Holy Spirit was right when He spoke to your fathers through Isaiah the prophet" (Acts 28:25); "as the Holy Spirit says", before Psalm 95 (Heb 3:7); Jesus reads "The Spirit of the Lord is on Me" (Isa 61:1) of himself (Luke 4:18); Peter calls Pentecost "what was spoken by the prophet Joel" (Acts 2:16), quoting "I will pour out My Spirit" (2:17); and the Hebrew Bible itself uses the words "Your Holy Spirit" (Ps 51:11) and "His Holy Spirit" (Isa 63:10). LEFT OPEN: the Hebrew Scriptures do not themselves make the identification, and "holy spirit" there may be read as God's own spirit; their word, ruach, is spirit, wind and breath, and Jewish readers have heard the phrase in several ways, often as God's own presence, power or breath. The site maker reads these as one Spirit; they are kept as two here so that each reader can weigh the text for themselves.
